correctness.rationale: At the predator-free state, derivatives of the prey-dependent birth and death rates multiply the zero predator density, so the linearization is triangular. The predator block is a scalar renewal equation and its exponential modes give the displayed characteristic equation. The modulus bound excludes right-half-plane roots when the reproduction integral is below one; above one the positive real characteristic function crosses one exactly once. The source's positive hunger mortality gives exponential tail control. The g-derivatives are strictly negative because the smooth juvenile weight has positive accumulated exposure at every positive age, while k enters fertility linearly. In the sharp limit, change of variables from age to adult age-since-maturation gives the exact exponential factor and the tau-star derivative is strictly negative.

value.rationale: The motivating study spends substantial computation on predator-free phase classification and identifies juvenile predation g and maturation age tau-star as the dominant controls. The result replaces the local predator-free boundary in each g sweep by an exact one-dimensional threshold, proves that boundary cannot re-enter, gives an explicit k trade-off, and in the sharp model proves a closed-form monotone g_c(tau-star). This turns a major numerical phase-boundary feature into a reusable analytic diagnostic while keeping coexistence dynamics outside the claim.
